svg.text: K11 Box shelf and lid station: the hand-over between the two carriages
The storage carriage brings a box through the ceiling port, the lid station takes its lid, the box waits on a stub carrier for the cell hand.
box shelf X 1860–2430, y 200–525, z 1550 · 3 carriers
bought GN 1/6 and 1/9 boxes, flat seal lid, no stub
FRONT VIEW of the S column, z 1350–2200
stub −y: the hand grips it from the rear
The storage gripper only touches box
rims and never covers an open box.
Lids come off in the dry shaft and wait
in the magazine; the same station
puts them back before the box returns.
• on the shelf, cams hold them open:
the storage gripper can set or take
• lifted by the hand, they snap shut
over the box rims: the hand can tip
the box over a pan or the cooker.
Raw (class R) boxes ride only on
the red carrier; after an R grip the
hand gets a 20 s hot sleeve rinse.
The controller admits one carriage at
a time over the shelf; the carriers

g.text: 1/7 The storage carriage drives over the port; the hoist lowers the box, the gripper pushes the spring flap open.
2/7 Lid station: the vacuum cup slides over the lid, the box drops 60 mm away from it, the lid goes to the magazine.
3/7 The open box goes down onto a green stub carrier; the shelf holds the carrier hooks open; the gripper lets go.
4/7 The storage carriage leaves the shared zone; the flap closes behind it.
5/7 The cell hand grips the carrier stub from the rear and lifts: the spring hooks snap shut over the box rims.
6/7 After tipping, the carrier comes back; on the shelf the hooks open again; the hand leaves.
7/7 The storage carriage takes the empty box, the cup puts a lid back on, the box returns to storage.
